title: VONKO-017: ‘Characteristics, treatment patterns and survival of individuals with prostate cancer - including metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) - a study based on cancer registry data’
summary:
Prostate cancer - incidence, treatment and new findings
Prostate cancer is the most common type of cancer in men in Germany. There were around 65,820 new cases in 2020. In terms of cancer deaths, prostate cancer is in second place. Older men are particularly affected, as the risk increases with age. Men over the age of 75 have a risk of up to 7% of developing prostate cancer in the next ten years.
Fortunately, thanks to modern diagnostic methods and treatments, the chances of survival are good: around 91% of those affected live for at least five years after diagnosis. However, if the cancer has already spread to other parts of the body (metastasised), this proportion drops to around 54%.

Treatment options
Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) plays a central role in the treatment of prostate cancer. This therapy aims to reduce the male hormone testosterone, which promotes the growth of prostate cancer cells. In many cases, ADT is combined with special drugs such as abiraterone, apalutamide or enzalutamide to make the treatment even more effective. The use of the chemotherapeutic agent docetaxel has also proven to be helpful.
However, in some cases prostate cancer becomes resistant to hormone therapy. This is known as castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). In such cases, drugs such as enzalutamide and abiraterone or chemotherapy with docetaxel and cabazitaxel are used. A promising new method is the so-called Lu-177-PSMA therapy, which specifically attacks cancer cells.

Important research for better treatments
Despite much progress, there are still unanswered questions about the best treatment for advanced prostate cancer. Our study investigates how prostate cancer patients in Germany are actually treated and what side effects or complications occur. The aim is to improve knowledge about the course of the disease and to further optimise care.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of cancer registry data of prostate cancer cases from the diagnosis years 2014-2024 (observational study)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. ICD-10 C61
2. Diagnosis years 2014-2024
3. Place of residence at diagnosis in the federal state of the requested registry (‘residence-related cases’)
4. At least one day survival / follow-up time
5. Minimum age of 18 years at diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
1. the case is known to the registry exclusively on the basis of 
a. a  death certificate (DCO case) 
b. a pathology report 
c. a progress report 
d. a report to the tumour conference 
e. a combination of the aforementioned notification types 
2. unknown vital status at the end of the follow-up period
3. patients who have experienced another cancer either up to 5 years before or within the time window up to 5 years after the diagnosis of prostate cancer (excluding non-melanotic skin tumours, ICD-10 C44)
